subject: Reults from scanmqm() were vastly different from scanone() and scantwo(). Are they valid/reliable?

messages.author: 9ddf1f5ad51e8c4f
messages.subject: Reults from scanmqm() were vastly different from scanone() and scantwo(). Are they valid/reliable?
parts:
Hi,

I'm trying to use multiple QTL mapping (scanmqm()) on a population of 178 recombinant inbred lines with 1221 markers. On average, my markers are about 1 cM apart.

I build an intial list of 153 cofactors from different autocofactors() runs as suggested by Danny Arends. (https://groups.google.com/forum/?utm_medium=email&utm_source=footer#!msg/rqtl-disc/Q1AJp7_6xDw/uloRef8nBQAJ) I specified that each pair of cofactors must be at least 5 cM apart, resulting in a list of 153 cofactors ready for scanmqm() to use (Fig. 1).

Fig.1 Genetic map with initial 153 cofactors for scanmqm() function marked as red dots.



Then I ran scanmqm() with that list and got LOD results that were vastly different from scanone(..., method = "ehk") results (Fig. 2).

Fig. 2 Comparison of LOD profiles from scanone() and scanmqm().



The MQM model that was returned from scanmqm consisted of 22 'QTLs' that, as I understand it, were used as covariate when testing for distant QTLs. 

Fig. 3 is the LOD profile from plotLodProfile() after running refineqtl() on the model returned by mqmscan().

Fig. 3 One-dimensional LOD profiles for each QTL from MQM model. Dotted line is genome-wide significance at alpha = 0.01 level from mqmpermutation().



However, when I used scantwo() function (Fig. 4), I could not detect any evidence for epistatic interactions, not even for the three QTLs I identified from scanone().

Fig. 4 Results from scantwo() function.



My questions are:

  1. Did I over fit the MQM model with 22 ramaining cofactor, given the population that I have (178 recombinant inbred lines, 175 of which were typed)? 
  2. For LOD profile around Q1 (overall MQM LOD profile, Fig. 2), did the MQM model used all Q2-Q22 as covariates and how did it do that given the population only consists of 175 typed RILs?
  3. How can there be so many more QTLs detected by MQM method whilst only three were detected from both scanone() abd scantwo()? Are the MQM results reliable?
  4. Are my mqmpermutation(..., cofactors = cof.mqm, scanfunction = mqmscan, method = "permutation", n.perm = 10000, n.cluster = 8) results a bit strange that there were only 10 unique maximum LOD scores and 10% of permutations were at the highest value of 3.639 whilst the highest LOD score from scanmqm() was 16.474. (LOD score distribution seen in Fig. 5)?

Fig. 5 Distribution of maximum LOD score from mqmpermutation().

messages.author: 92292fc48bf46044
messages.subject: Re: Reults from scanmqm() were vastly different from scanone() and scantwo(). Are they valid/reliable?
parts: My answers are under your questions:

My questions are:

  1. Did I over fit the MQM model with 22 ramaining cofactor, given the population that I have (178 recombinant inbred lines, 175 of which were typed)?

No in theory not. The MQM routine can handle upto (n individuals - 10) = ~ 165 cofactors, with 155 you're below this theorectical threshold,
However,I would not go that high. My advice is to take ~ 100 cofactors into the model selection phase to prevent overfitting
1. For LOD profile around Q1 (overall MQM LOD profile, Fig. 2), did the MQM model used all Q2-Q22 as covariates and how did it do that given the population only consists of 175 typed RILs?

Yes, this is exactly what the MQM routine does. MQM compensates for all other cofactors, in your case you loose 21 out of
174 degrees of freedom in the statistical test, this is perfectly reasonable
1. How can there be so many more QTLs detected by MQM method whilst only three were detected from both scanone() abd scantwo()? Are the MQM results reliable?

scanone does not compensate for the cofactors used in the model, this is why MQM has higher statistical power to detect effects.
However you should adjust the threshold using permutations where you include the same number of initial cofactors, my guess is
that your scanone defined threshold is too low for the MQM routine.

1. Are my mqmpermutation(..., cofactors = cof.mqm, scanfunction = mqmscan, method = "permutation", n.perm = 10000, n.cluster = 8) results a bit strange that there were only 10 unique maximum LOD scores and 10% of permutations were at the highest value of 3.639 whilst the highest LOD score from scanmqm() was 16.474. (LOD score distribution seen in Fig. 5)?

this is really worrisome, I think something goes wrong in the permutation routine (too many initial cofactors), or the phenotype that you're mapping is not a normal distribution

If you want me too look into this please send me a copy of your data set (will be handled confidentially) per email: Danny....@gmail.com

Kind regards,
Danny
